_about: Programmes Talaash Heritage runs on request. Edited in the repository, not in the admin page.

details.How it works: Tell us what you want to discuss and we agree a time that suits you

programmes.title: Mehrauli Archaeological Park
programmes.subtitle: A thousand years of building in one walk
programmes.description:
From Rajon ki Baoli to Balban's tomb and Jamali Kamali, the park holds remains from the eleventh century to the British period. An archaeologist shows you how to tell one period's masonry and arches from another's.

Give us your date and your group, and we set the start time, the pace and the language to suit. Entry tickets, where a site charges them, are extra.

details.For: Schools, colleges, companies and the public
details.Group size: About 10 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: The Qutb complex
programmes.subtitle: Reading a World Heritage Site stone by stone
programmes.description:
The Qutb Minar stands beside a mosque built with reused temple pillars, an iron pillar of the Gupta period, and the Alai Darwaza of 1311. We read the inscriptions and the joints in the masonry to follow how the complex grew.

Give us your date and your group, and we set the start time, the pace and the language to suit. Entry tickets, where a site charges them, are extra.

details.For: Schools, colleges, companies and the public
details.Group size: About 10 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Purana Qila
programmes.subtitle: A sixteenth-century fort and the dig beneath it
programmes.description:
Humayun and Sher Shah built the fort. Archaeologists have excavated inside it several times since the 1950s and found settlement going back more than two thousand years. We walk the walls and look at what came out of the trenches.

Give us your date and your group, and we set the start time, the pace and the language to suit. Entry tickets, where a site charges them, are extra.

details.Group size: About 10 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Hauz Khas
programmes.subtitle: A medieval college beside a royal reservoir
programmes.description:
Alauddin Khalji dug the reservoir for his city of Siri. Firoz Shah Tughlaq later built a madrasa along its edge and his own tomb at the corner. The walk covers how the college worked and how to recognise Tughlaq building.

Give us your date and your group, and we set the start time, the pace and the language to suit. Entry tickets, where a site charges them, are extra.

details.For: Schools, colleges, companies and the public
details.Group size: About 10 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Museum morning with an archaeologist
programmes.subtitle: One gallery, looked at properly
programmes.description:
Most visitors pass a thousand objects in an hour and remember none. We choose one gallery with you and spend the morning on a dozen objects: what each is, how it was made and found, and what it tells us.

Give us your date and your group, and we choose the gallery, the pace and the language to suit. Museum entry is extra.
programmes.venue: A Delhi museum chosen with you

details.For: Schools, colleges, companies and the public
details.Group size: About 10 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Culture and heritage: what we inherit and why it matters
programmes.subtitle: An illustrated talk for students and teams new to the subject
programmes.description:
What counts as culture, what counts as heritage, and how the two differ. We work through tangible and intangible heritage with Indian examples, then look at who protects it: UNESCO, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the people who live beside a monument.

Length, level and language are set with you. It runs online or at your venue, for a class, a department or a whole team.

details.Group size: About 25 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: What archaeologists actually do
programmes.subtitle: How a site is found, dug, recorded and looked after
programmes.description:
From the first survey to the museum shelf. Students see how a site is located, how a trench is laid out and recorded, what happens to finds in the laboratory, and what becomes of a site once the dig is over.

Length, level and language are set with you. It runs online or at your venue, for a class, a department or a whole team.

details.Group size: About 25 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: From stone tools to the first villages
programmes.subtitle: Human origins and the Stone Age in South Asia
programmes.description:
How early people lived in the subcontinent, told through the tools they left behind. We follow the story from handaxes to microliths to the first farming settlements, using photographs of real finds.

Length, level and language are set with you. It runs online or at your venue, for a class, a department or a whole team.

details.Group size: About 25 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: The first cities: Harappa among the early civilisations
programmes.subtitle: Mesopotamia, Egypt, China and the Indus compared
programmes.description:
What made a city more than four thousand years ago: planning, drains, weights, seals and trade. We set the Harappan cities beside Mesopotamia, Egypt and early China, so students see what the four shared and what belonged to the Indus world alone.

Length, level and language are set with you. It runs online or at your venue, for a class, a department or a whole team.

details.Group size: About 25 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Reading India's scripts: Brāhmī to Śāradā
programmes.subtitle: A lecture and demonstration with real inscriptions
programmes.description:
Most scripts used in India today descend from Brāhmī, the script of Aśoka's edicts. We trace that family on screen, read a line of an edict together, and show how epigraphists date an inscription from the shape of its letters.

Length, level and language are set with you. It runs online or at your venue, for a class, a department or a whole team.

details.Group size: About 25 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: How to read a temple
programmes.subtitle: Nāgara, Drāviḍa and Vesara in one evening
programmes.description:
A plan, an elevation and a handful of terms are enough to start reading a temple. We compare the northern, southern and Deccan traditions with photographs and drawings, so the next temple you visit makes sense from the gateway to the sanctum.

Length, level and language are set with you. It runs online or at your venue, for a class, a department or a whole team.

details.Group size: About 25 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: India's linguistic heritage
programmes.subtitle: The language families of the subcontinent and how they met
programmes.description:
India's languages belong to several families that have borrowed from one another for thousands of years. This talk maps them, explains how linguists reconstruct their history, and looks at what is lost when a language stops being spoken.

Length, level and language are set with you. It runs online or at your venue, for a class, a department or a whole team.

details.Group size: About 25 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Rock art of India
programmes.subtitle: Painted shelters and engraved rocks, and how they are recorded
programmes.description:
From the painted shelters of Bhimbetka to the engravings of the Konkan coast, India is rich in rock art. We look at what the images show, how they are dated, and how researchers document them before they fade.

Length, level and language are set with you. It runs online or at your venue, for a class, a department or a whole team.

details.Group size: About 25 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: The goddess in text and image: the Devīmāhātmya
programmes.subtitle: The text behind Navarātri
programmes.description:
The Devīmāhātmya is the best-known Sanskrit text on the Goddess and is still recited every Navarātri. We read key passages in translation and set them beside sculpture and painting to see how the Śākta tradition took shape.

Length, level and language are set with you. It runs online or at your venue, for a class, a department or a whole team.

details.Group size: About 25 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Careers in archaeology, museums and heritage
programmes.subtitle: A group session for students choosing what to study
programmes.description:
What the work is, which degrees lead to it, and where the jobs are. Students leave with a map of courses, entrance routes and first steps, and there is time for their own questions.

Length, level and language are set with you. It runs online or at your venue, for a class, a department or a whole team.

details.Group size: About 25 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Mock trench: a practice excavation
programmes.subtitle: Students dig, record and interpret a prepared trench
programmes.description:
We build a trench with layers and planted finds. Students excavate with real tools, record what they find and where, and then argue out what happened at the site.

We bring the materials and fit the session to your space, your timetable and the age of the group.
programmes.venue: Your campus, outdoors or in sand trays

details.Group size: About 20 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Clay and the past: a pottery workshop
programmes.subtitle: Make a pot, then learn to read one
programmes.description:
Pottery is the most common find on an excavation. Participants shape clay by hand, then sort replica sherds the way archaeologists do: by fabric, form and decoration.

We bring the materials and fit the session to your space, your timetable and the age of the group.

details.Group size: About 20 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Reading sculpture
programmes.subtitle: A talk, a gallery or temple visit, and a quiz
programmes.description:
Who is this figure, and how do we know? After a short illustrated talk, students study sculpture in a museum gallery or at a temple, identify figures from what they hold and wear, and finish with a quiz.

We bring the materials and fit the session to your space, your timetable and the age of the group.
programmes.venue: A museum or temple near you

details.Group size: About 20 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Write like Aśoka's scribes: a Brāhmī workshop
programmes.subtitle: Learn the letters and write your own name
programmes.description:
Brāhmī is more than two thousand years old and simple enough to begin in an afternoon. Participants learn the letters, write their names, and read a few words from a real edict.

We bring the materials and fit the session to your space, your timetable and the age of the group.
programmes.venue: Your campus or office, or online

details.For: Schools, colleges, companies and the public
details.Group size: About 20 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Recording the past: a documentation workshop
programmes.subtitle: How to record a site and an object properly
programmes.description:
A find without a record is only an old object. Participants fill in a context sheet, draw and photograph an object to scale, and write a catalogue entry, using the formats we use in our own projects.

We bring the materials and fit the session to your space, your timetable and the age of the group.

details.Length: Half a day or a full day
details.Group size: About 20 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Caring for collections: preventive conservation basics
programmes.subtitle: Paper, textiles and metal, for anyone who looks after old things
programmes.description:
Most damage to a collection comes from light, damp, pests and handling, and most of it can be prevented cheaply. A conservator shows how to assess, store and handle paper, textiles and metal, with practice on sample materials.

We bring the materials and fit the session to your space, your timetable and the age of the group.

details.For: Colleges, museums, archives and company collections
details.Group size: About 20 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Stone tools up close
programmes.subtitle: How early tools were made, used and classified
programmes.description:
A prehistorian demonstrates how stone tools were struck and what the scars on them mean. Participants sort tool types, handle replicas and learn the first steps of lithic analysis.

We bring the materials and fit the session to your space, your timetable and the age of the group.

details.Group size: About 20 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: The dig: an archaeology team challenge
programmes.subtitle: A half-day team activity for workplaces
programmes.description:
Teams compete to excavate, record and interpret a prepared trench, then present their reading of the evidence. It rewards careful observation and clear reporting more than speed.

We bring the materials and fit the session to your space, your timetable and the age of the group.
programmes.venue: Your office or an offsite venue

details.Group size: About 20 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Prakrit: a first course
programmes.subtitle: Read the language of India's earliest inscriptions
programmes.description:
Prakrit was the everyday speech of much of ancient India and the language of Aśoka's edicts. The course covers the basics of grammar and guided reading of short passages.

We run it for your batch on dates you choose. Timing, pace and assessment are agreed before it starts.

details.For: Colleges, study circles and the public
details.Group size: About 15 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Pali: a first course
programmes.subtitle: Begin reading the language of the Theravāda Buddhist canon
programmes.description:
The course covers pronunciation, basic grammar and the reading of short passages, and ends with a test for those who want one.

We run it for your batch on dates you choose. Timing, pace and assessment are agreed before it starts.

details.For: Colleges, study circles and the public
details.Length: Evening sessions, number agreed with you
details.Group size: About 15 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Śāradā script
programmes.subtitle: Learn to read the script of Kashmir's manuscripts
programmes.description:
Participants learn the alphabet, conjuncts and numerals, practise transliteration, and read from manuscript pages.

We run it for your batch on dates you choose. Timing, pace and assessment are agreed before it starts.

details.For: Colleges, study circles and the public
details.Group size: About 15 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Understanding Indian temple architecture
programmes.subtitle: Four evenings on temple forms and how they developed
programmes.description:
A basic introduction: the parts of a temple, the regional styles and their antiquity, and the ways scholars approach architecture. A certificate of completion can be issued.

We run it for your batch on dates you choose. Timing, pace and assessment are agreed before it starts.

details.For: Colleges, study circles and the public
details.Length: Four sessions, about 4.5 hours in all
details.Group size: About 15 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Remote sensing in archaeology and heritage management
programmes.subtitle: A three-month certificate course
programmes.description:
How satellite images, aerial photographs and mapping software are used to find, map and monitor sites. Live weekend sessions, with recordings for anyone who misses one.

We run it for your batch on dates you choose. Timing, pace and assessment are agreed before it starts.

details.Group size: About 15 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Martial arts and society
programmes.subtitle: Three evenings on wrestling, combat and culture in Indian history
programmes.description:
What sculpture, texts and living traditions tell us about wrestling and combat sports in India, and what they meant to the people who practised and paid for them.

We run it for your batch on dates you choose. Timing, pace and assessment are agreed before it starts.

details.For: Colleges, study circles and the public
details.Group size: About 15 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.

programmes.title: Museum field school: documentation and conservation
programmes.subtitle: A week of supervised work on a real collection
programmes.description:
Participants document, clean and rehouse objects from a museum collection under conservators and documentation specialists, with daily laboratory sessions, lectures and visits to nearby sites. It suits students of conservation, museology, archaeology and related fields.

Dates, location and syllabus are agreed with your institution. You receive a day-by-day plan and a quotation before you commit.

details.Group size: About 35 works well. Smaller and larger groups can be discussed.
details.Itinerary: Day-by-day plan shared before you commit

programmes.title: Prehistory field workshop
programmes.subtitle: Three days of survey, stone tools, rock art and megaliths
programmes.description:
A field introduction to prehistory: reading the local landscape, finding and classifying stone tools, documenting rock art and megaliths, and taking samples.

Dates, location and syllabus are agreed with your institution. You receive a day-by-day plan and a quotation before you commit.

programmes.title: Three capitals: Delhi, Agra and Jaipur
programmes.subtitle: The Golden Triangle as a study tour
programmes.description:
An archaeologist travels with the group and uses Delhi's Sultanate monuments, Mughal Agra and Fatehpur Sikri, and eighteenth-century Jaipur to show how three courts built their capitals.

You receive a day-by-day itinerary and a quotation before you commit. Route, pace, stay and budget are adjusted until they suit your group.

programmes.title: Forts of Rajasthan
programmes.subtitle: A study tour of the hill forts and the states that built them
programmes.description:
Six of Rajasthan's hill forts are on the World Heritage list. The tour covers how the forts were sited, supplied with water and defended, with a historian travelling alongside.

You receive a day-by-day itinerary and a quotation before you commit. Route, pace, stay and budget are adjusted until they suit your group.

programmes.title: Stupas, caves and temples of central India
programmes.subtitle: Sanchi, Udayagiri, Bhimbetka and Khajuraho
programmes.description:
Four sites in Madhya Pradesh that cover rock art, early Buddhist architecture, Gupta sculpture and the medieval temple at its height. An archaeologist leads, and reading is sent in advance.
